title: The Pulse, Tuesday 8 October 2026
tldr: Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 both dropped yesterday. Haiku 5.5 costs 75% less than Haiku 4.5 with a 1M context window, tuned for subagents and high-volume work. GPT-6 rolls out with Intelligent UI, delivering interactive visual experiences in ChatGPT.

models.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
models.summary: Anthropic's small, fast model for high-volume work with 1M context window, 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5.
models.why: Ideal subagent for our LangChain pipelines, code review compactions, and EverRaise high-volume SMS/call summaries.

models.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
models.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 rolls out globally in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, delivering faster responses with interactive visual experiences.
models.why: Worth knowing for customer conversations and benchmarking our DSPy chains against frontier models, no direct use for us yet.

research.title: Humanize: Judgement Engineering for Agentic Coding
research.summary: Multi-agent orchestration workflow for agentic coding built around explicit, mechanically enforced decisions at planning and implementation boundaries.
research.why: Directly applicable to our Claude Code and Hermes workflows—the judgement boundary pattern addresses the weak-judge problem we see in code review panels.

research.title: How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? A Tool-Call Vector Shaped by Suppression
research.summary: Identifies a tool-call decision vector shaped by suppression mechanisms in agentic prompts with tool schemas.
research.why: Explains tool-calling behavior in our DSPy programs and Hermes; understanding suppression can improve prompt design for Vapi agents and LangChain tools.

research.title: Whose Memory Is It? Scope-Aware Commit Rules for Long-Term LLM Memory
research.summary: Persistent memory with scope-aware commit rules to prevent deliberation artifacts from becoming durable facts.
research.why: Hermes memory (Mnemosyne) and SalesKick conversation state both need this—prevents simulated tool results or rejected plans from polluting long-term context.

research.title: ToolRACER: A Robust Agentic Conversation Emulation Resource for Agent Training and Evaluation
research.summary: Benchmark for function-calling agents emphasizing adversarial and non-cooperative conversation trajectories.
research.why: EverRaise agents on Vapi handle real users who don't follow scripts; ToolRACER's adversarial eval matches what we need for SalesKick coaching quality.

releases.title: Node.js v26.11.0 (Current)
releases.summary: Notable additions include Buffer.isLatin1, Buffer.stringLength(), and http isValidHeaderName() and isValidHeaderValue() methods.
releases.why: Current release for our Node services; the new Buffer and HTTP validation methods are useful for EverRaise API handlers and Vapi webhooks.

releases.title: Next.js v16.4.0
releases.summary: Stable release with bundle analyzer historical snapshots, proxy detection fixes, and Turbopack resolveAlias improvements.
releases.why: Stable upgrade path for SalesKick dashboard and Chrysalis; bundle analyzer snapshots will help track client bundle growth over time.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.54.0
releases.summary: Adds trace topic classification, external media storage integration, and session transcript views.
releases.why: We use Langfuse to trace DSPy programs and LangChain pipelines; topic classification will help us segment SalesKick call types and Pipeline retrieval patterns.

hackernews.title: Margaret Hamilton has died
hackernews.summary: Margaret Hamilton, who led Apollo software development and coined 'software engineering,' has died.
hackernews.why: Worth remembering the engineer who built the systems that got us to the moon; her rigor shaped what we still call software engineering.

hackernews.title: Docker Agent
hackernews.summary: Docker's official agent for container orchestration and management automation.
hackernews.why: Relevant for Pipeline's Railway deployments and potential local dev automation in our Docker-based services.

hackernews.title: Shipping JPEG XL in Chrome
hackernews.summary: Chrome ships JPEG XL support, offering better compression and quality than legacy formats.
hackernews.why: Reduces image bandwidth for SalesKick dashboard and Chrysalis; JPEG XL can improve load times for media-heavy pages.

hackernews.title: Hackers obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large services
hackernews.summary: Attackers obtained counterfeit TLS certificates for major services, exposing certificate authority compromise.
hackernews.why: Security reminder for our services on Railway and Vercel; certificate pinning and monitoring become more critical.

x_posts.title: ClaudeDevs on Haiku 5.5 availability
x_posts.summary: Haiku 5.5 is now available in Claude Platform and Claude Code, costs 75% less than Haiku 4.5, pairs well with Opus or Sonnet as a subagent.
x_posts.why: Confirms subagent use case for Hermes and our multi-model code review panels; the cost savings make high-volume tracing and compaction viable.

x_posts.title: Nous Research raises Series B
x_posts.summary: Nous Research raised a Series B to bring Hermes Agent to new frontiers and build a mobile app, reported in the Wall Street Journal.
x_posts.why: Hermes is our primary agent tool; the funding and mobile roadmap signal continued investment in the platform we rely on for code review and automation.

x_posts.title: ClaudeDevs on computer use in SDKs
x_posts.summary: Computer use and browser use toolsets are now built into Claude's Python and TypeScript SDKs with a managed loop for clicks and keystrokes.
x_posts.why: Simplifies browser automation for our Hermes desktop workflows and any future Claude-powered testing or scraping tasks.

x_posts.title: Addy Osmani on Haiku 5.5 as subagent
x_posts.summary: Addy Osmani's team uses Haiku 5.5 as a subagent alongside Opus 5.5 for cheap, fast, capable small-model work.
x_posts.why: Validates the subagent pattern we use in code review panels; confirms Haiku 5.5 + Opus 5.5 is a viable pair for multi-tier agent architectures.
